Once I start, I need to get drunk. I have zero control after the first drink. Can I cut back by starting drinking later in the day? Or do I just need to quit cold turkey?
Is it possible to cut back to quit?
My opinion would be don't drink at all, but I'm an asshole sometimes, so take my advice with that in mind. lol
If you start drinking later in the day, what makes you think that the need to get drunk after one drink will disappear? You'll probably fulfill your compulsion to get drunk by staying up later.

Anything is possible. Everyone quits in a different way. Make the attempt. If it doesn't work, the try cold turkey. Unless you are a real heavy drinker, in which case, stopping cold turkey without medical assistance could be dangerous. The important thing is to quit if it is causing you problems or if you no longer want to drink.

Later on in the day could possibly help if you're flexible. For example, if you want to cut back, buy an amount less than you normally drink, then time it so you finish that when liquor sales stop for the night around 2am (or your local law time). Then there is nothing you can do to get more drunk.

Well, hopefully nothing you can do.

Edit: also to add that starting later can easily lead to more problems, like still getting drunk and resulting in less sleep, missing work, etc.

Depending on your consumption level, quitting cold turkey can be dangerous to your health and leave you vulnerable to seizures and other complications. You should consult with a doctor to avoid this and decide the healthiest route.

If you're like me starting later just means you will stay up later drinking until you reach blackout. In my experience my attempts to moderate were unsuccessful. Living without sounds scary but after the initial rough period your life will improve exponentially. We are all here to support! Good luck and don't hesitate to ask for more help/information.
I had to quit cold turkey. Cutting back did not cut it for me- all or nothing for me.

I'm know where you're coming from, once I start, I don't usually stop. I feel like there is a correlation with how quickly I consume that first drink. If I drink it very slowly, the probability that it's my only drink that day greatly increases. Just a thought. Good luck to you!

A blogger faces up to 2 years in jail and $50,000NZD in fines for ‘trolling' as New Zealand's first trial under the Harmful Digital Communications Bill goes to court this week. The bill, which passed mid-2015, has raised concerns with vague legislation, outlawing “causing harm by posting digital communication”.

Online freelance journalist, Don Foqu’dup, stands accused after posted an article to his website regarding his local drug store promoting alternate medicines and "being the soul-sucking cancer on society". Foqu’dup later removed the article but not before it received attention on social media where it was seen by the drug store’s owner, Ira Tional.

Tional had this to say in a statement to the press: “This has hurt my reputation and business. The personal harassment deeply concerned my wife and I, needless to say, the effects will be with us for the rest of our lives."

Due to a coinciding amendment to the New Zealand's Crimes Act in 2015, part of the article, where it was suggested that the world would be better off if Trional "could go […] and overdose on his homeopathic remedies”, may see Foqu’dup also face an additional third year in prison for encouraging another person’s suicide.

When approached for comment Foqu’dup asked “Are they fucking kidding me?”
